page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 64 vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and a base frequency of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core, alongside 3780 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core performance, with the PassMark CPU score and static web serving throughput ranking in the top 10% tier. Single-core stress-ng performance and PassMark memory scores sit in the average range, but multi-threaded operations show high efficiency, as evidenced by top-tier bzip3 decompression and strong multi-core stress-ng results. The platform also demonstrates strong memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, alongside high-throughput capabilities in Redis SET operations and small-model LLM prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D64ds_v7 offers a dense allocation of compute and memory resources coupled with substantial local storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for high-I/O operations. This resource balance makes the server highly suitable for database hosting, static web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and lightweight LLM inference workloads.
